_comment: GENERATED from src/lib/catalog.ts by scripts/gen-catalog.ts - do not hand-edit. Regenerate: npm run gen:catalog

entries.name: Citrix Workspace
entries.note: Self-extracting; the switches live in the inner bootstrapper. Add /includeSSON for pass-through SSO, and ADDLOCAL="ReceiverInside,ICA_Client,USB,DesktopViewer,WebHelper" to pick components.

entries.name: Microsoft Teams (new, machine-wide)
entries.note: Not an MSI and not in Add/Remove Programs: -p PROVISIONS the Teams MSIX for every user on the machine (check with Get-AppxProvisionedPackage -Online, DisplayName MSTeams). Plain -p downloads the MSIX from Microsoft at install time; -o points it at a local MSTeams-x64.msix instead, which is what you want for a deployment tool or a machine without open internet. -x removes the provisioned package. Windows 11 often already has MSTeams provisioned; the bootstrapper replaces it.

entries.name: Microsoft Teams (classic machine-wide)
entries.note: The machine-wide MSI only PROVISIONS a per-user install at each logon. New Teams uses teamsbootstrapper.exe -p instead.

entries.name: AnyDesk
entries.note: Custom CLI (not MSI-style). --install REQUIRES the target folder as an argument.

entries.name: Docker Desktop
entries.note: Sub-command style (install/uninstall as a verb, not a slash flag). --accept-license is required for unattended.

entries.name: Adobe Acrobat Reader
entries.note: /sAll silent, /rs suppress reboot, /msi forwards the rest to the inner MSI. EULA_ACCEPT=YES is mandatory.

entries.name: CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor
entries.note: CID (customer ID + checksum) is REQUIRED - without it the sensor installs but never registers.

entries.name: Python
entries.note: Custom bootstrapper; properties are bare NAME=value (no slash). Add Include_test=0 to skip the test suite.

entries.name: Visual Studio Code
entries.note: Use the SYSTEM installer (VSCodeSetup-x64-*.exe). The download page and winget default to the USER installer (VSCodeUserSetup-*), which run as SYSTEM installs into SYSTEM's own profile - exit 0, and no real user ever sees it. Inno Setup: /MERGETASKS=!runcode stops it launching after install; add addcontextmenufiles,addtopath for shell integration + PATH.

entries.name: Git for Windows
entries.note: Inno Setup. Use /LOADINF="config.inf" to preset components/options (record one with /SAVEINF).

entries.name: Zoom Outlook Plugin
entries.note: A separate MSI from the Zoom client, so a Zoom rule will not deploy it. It installed and uninstalled cleanly on a VM with no Outlook present, so deploying it ahead of Office is safe.

entries.name: Zoom
entries.note: Use the MSI (not the per-user exe) for fleet deploys; pass ZConfig/ZoomAutoUpdate properties for config.

entries.name: Oracle VM VirtualBox
entries.note: Qt-based custom installer. --silent + --ignore-reboot; the network-driver install can still prompt unless the Oracle cert is pre-trusted in the cert store.

entries.name: Wireshark
entries.note: NSIS. Bundles Npcap, which runs its own installer - add /quiet and let it through.

entries.name: TeamViewer (Host)
entries.note: Add APITOKEN=<token> CUSTOMCONFIGID=<id> ASSIGNMENTOPTIONS="..." to auto-assign the Host to your account.

entries.name: GlobalProtect (Palo Alto VPN)
entries.note: PORTAL= preconfigures the gateway so users aren't prompted.

entries.name: Microsoft 365 Apps / Office
entries.note: Office has NO plain silent switch - it installs via the Office Deployment Tool (setup.exe) driven by a config.xml. Author the XML at config.office.com (channel, bitness, apps, language), ship it next to setup.exe. "{file} /download config.xml" pre-stages the bits first.

entries.name: Adobe Acrobat (Pro / Standard)
entries.note: Same flags as Reader (/sAll silent, /rs suppress reboot, /msi forwards to the inner MSI; EULA_ACCEPT=YES mandatory). Volume licensing comes from the package built in the Adobe Admin Console, not a command-line key.

entries.name: Foxit PDF Editor
entries.note: KEYCODE= (your volume license) is REQUIRED to activate - without it it installs as an unlicensed trial. Add MAKEDEFAULT=0 so it doesn't grab the PDF association.

entries.name: Nitro PDF Pro
entries.note: SERIALNUMBER= is REQUIRED to activate; without it you get trial mode.

entries.name: TechSmith Snagit
entries.note: TSC_SOFTWARE_KEY= the software key. TechSmith's Deployment Tool emits an .mst - apply it with TRANSFORMS="snagit.mst" to also kill auto-update + the welcome screen.

entries.name: Webroot SecureAnywhere
entries.note: Tiny stub installer; /key= (your 20-char keycode) is REQUIRED to register the endpoint, /silent suppresses UI. Add /lockautouninstall=<password> to require a password to remove it.

entries.name: RustDesk
entries.note: Custom double-dash CLI (not MSI-style). --silent-install installs + registers the service. Drop a RustDesk2.toml beside the exe to preconfigure the relay/key.

entries.name: ESET Endpoint Security
entries.note: Bare MSI installs the client but it won't be MANAGED - for unattended enrollment layer the ESET PROTECT config (a generated .mst / install_config.ini) via TRANSFORMS=. A reboot is usually required.

entries.name: Google Chrome (Enterprise)
entries.note: Use the Enterprise MSI, not the consumer stub exe, for fleet deploys.

entries.name: Mozilla Firefox
entries.note: NSIS. Drop a policies.json / use the MSI for managed settings.

entries.name: Notepad++
entries.note: NSIS. /allusers installs machine-wide (HKLM, Program Files); drop it for a per-user install.

entries.name: OBS Studio
entries.note: NSIS.

entries.name: GIMP
entries.note: Inno Setup, and /VERYSILENT alone is NOT enough. Like Greenshot, GIMP shows the Inno "Select Setup Install Mode" dialog, presented BEFORE the silent machinery engages - no /SILENT flag suppresses it. Without /ALLUSERS it hangs forever under a deployment tool (session 0 has nobody to click it). Verified installing machine-wide with these switches. It is also SLOW - roughly 9 minutes for the ~300 MB payload - so raise your deployment timeout above the usual 5-minute default or the job is killed mid-install.

entries.name: FileZilla
entries.note: NSIS. /S suppresses the wizard; the bundled-offer screens are skipped by the official silent setup.

entries.name: PuTTY
entries.note: MSI (the .exe on the download page is the program itself, not an installer - grab the 64-bit MSI).

entries.name: Audacity
entries.note: Inno Setup.

entries.name: Postman
entries.note: Enterprise MSI only (the consumer build is a per-user .exe). INSTALLDIR sets a custom path.

entries.name: Foxit PDF Reader
entries.note: Vendor docs use /quiet. CLEAN="1" on uninstall also removes registry + user data. ADDLOCAL="FX_PDFVIEWER" installs the viewer only.

entries.name: Sumatra PDF
entries.note: Custom installer - NOT an MSI and NOT NSIS, so /S and /qn both do nothing. The documented "-install -s" is a PER-USER install (into %LocalAppData%) - under a deployment tool that means the SYSTEM profile, and no real user ever sees it. Even -all-users alone, run as SYSTEM, still put the program in SYSTEM's profile in our lab (3.6.1); pinning the folder with -d is what made it machine-wide. Add -no-desktop-shortcut on 3.7+.

entries.name: Greenshot
entries.note: Inno Setup, and /VERYSILENT alone is NOT enough. The installer shows a "Select Setup Install Mode" dialog that no /SILENT flag suppresses - without /ALLUSERS it hangs forever under a deployment tool (session 0 has nobody to click it). Also: the silent install OPENS THE GREENSHOT WEBSITE in a browser when it finishes and there is no switch to stop it, confirmed by the maintainers. Add /MERGETASKS="!startup" to skip the run-at-startup entry. No uninstall string is published: the vendor-registered unins000.exe /SILENT hung indefinitely as SYSTEM in testing, and a hanging uninstall is worse than none.

entries.name: LibreOffice
entries.note: Standard MSI. Add REGISTER_ALL_MSO_TYPES=1 to take over Office file associations, or REGISTER_NO_MSO_TYPES=1 to leave them alone.

entries.name: PowerShell 7
entries.note: Use the MSI, not winget's default: since 7.6 winget installs the per-user MSIX, which has no remoting endpoint and no $PSHOME config. Microsoft has said there is no MSI from 7.7 onward, so pin to the 7.6 LTS MSI for machine-wide deploys. Every 7.x installs into ...\PowerShell\7, so a newer MSI replaces the old one in place.

entries.name: Eclipse Temurin JDK
entries.note: JAVA_HOME is NOT set by default - FeatureJavaHome has to be in ADDLOCAL. Listing ADDLOCAL replaces the defaults, so keep FeatureMain in it. Skip ADDLOCAL=ALL (what winget uses): it adds FeatureOracleJavaSoft, which rewrites the HKLM JavaSoft keys and can hijack an existing Oracle Java. The install folder carries the build number (jdk-21.0.12.101-hotspot for 21.0.12.1+1), so detect on a fixed INSTALLDIR rather than the default path.

entries.name: KeePassXC
entries.note: Two properties default ON: LAUNCHAPPONEXIT starts the app when the install finishes, and AUTOSTARTPROGRAM adds a run-at-logon entry for every user. Set both to 0 for a quiet fleet deploy. Needs the VC++ 2015-2022 x64 runtime.

entries.name: Microsoft PowerToys (machine-wide)
entries.note: Two installers: PowerToysSetup-*.exe is machine-wide, PowerToysUserSetup-*.exe is per-user - and winget picks the per-user one unless you pass --scope machine. WiX Burn bundle, so the uninstall needs the SAME version's bundle (Burn also caches it under C:\ProgramData\Package Cache). Don't mix the per-user and machine installs on one PC. It installs the WebView2 runtime if missing and then self-updates.

entries.name: Google Drive for desktop
entries.note: Machine-wide (Program Files\Google\Drive File Stream) and installs a virtual-drive filesystem driver. Without --skip_launch_new it launches straight after install; --gsuite_shortcuts=false skips the Docs/Sheets/Slides Start-menu shortcuts. No stable uninstall string: the uninstaller sits in a versioned folder (Drive File Stream\<version>\uninstall.exe --silent --force_stop), so read it from the ARP entry at uninstall time. Grab the evergreen GoogleDriveSetup.exe from dl.google.com rather than a versioned URL.

entries.name: WireGuard
entries.note: The client UI launches after install unless DO_NOT_LAUNCH=1. Installs the WireGuardNT network driver. Tunnels are added afterwards, e.g. wireguard.exe /installtunnelservice C:\path\wg0.conf. Only Administrators can drive the UI unless you enable the LimitedOperatorUI policy for Network Configuration Operators.

entries.name: Tailscale
entries.note: The GUI launches after install unless TS_NOLAUNCH has any value. There is NO auth-key MSI property - despite what some guides say, the device still has to join your tailnet afterwards, e.g. tailscale up --auth-key=<key>. Set TS_UNATTENDEDMODE=always so the tunnel stays up with nobody logged on.

entries.name: KeePass Password Safe
entries.note: Use the MSI for fleet deploys (the Setup.exe alternative is Inno Setup: {file} /VERYSILENT /ALLUSERS). Options go through one property, KPS_OPTIONS - a comma list where a leading ! turns an option off. Downloads come via SourceForge, which serves an HTML page instead of the file to some scripted downloaders - check you actually got a ~3 MB MSI before you package it.

entries.name: WinSCP
entries.note: Inno Setup. /ALLUSERS matters: winget's default is a per-user install into %LocalAppData%. Machine-wide it lands in Program Files (x86)\WinSCP even on 64-bit Windows - the uninstall path above is the one we saw. The silent uninstall keeps saved sessions and settings. A WinSCP-*.msi also exists for msiexec /qn shops.

entries.name: Cisco Webex
entries.note: ACCEPT_EULA=TRUE spares every user the licence prompt, and ALLUSERS=1 is what makes it machine-wide (into Program Files\Cisco Spark) - without it the MSI installs per-user. Webex starts with Windows by default; AUTOSTART_WITH_WINDOWS=false turns that off (and locks the user's toggle). The file is always named Webex.msi, so keep track of the version separately.

entries.name: Microsoft Power BI Desktop
entries.note: ACCEPT_EULA=1 is mandatory - without it an unattended install fails. WiX Burn bundle: it registers two ARP entries (the bundle and its MSI), and the uninstall needs the same month's bundle (Burn also caches it under C:\ProgramData\Package Cache). Slow: ~11 minutes in our lab, so raise a 5-minute deployment timeout. Can't coexist with the Microsoft Store version. New release every month.

entries.name: Miniconda
entries.note: NSIS with case-sensitive switches. /D= must be LAST and UNQUOTED (even with spaces) - put it anywhere else and it is ignored. The default is /InstallationType=JustMe, the per-user trap. /AddToPath is ignored for AllUsers installs (disabled for security since 4.12), so add the PATH entry yourself if you need it. Licensing: Anaconda's default channels need a paid licence for organisations of 200+ people - point conda at conda-forge if that applies.

entries.name: Mozilla Thunderbird
entries.note: NSIS, same installer framework as Firefox. Quote the file - the vendor names it "Thunderbird Setup <version>.exe", with spaces. It also installs the Mozilla Maintenance Service (pass /MaintenanceService=false to skip it); the uninstall above removed both in our lab. Other switches: /DesktopShortcut=false, /TaskbarShortcut=false, /InstallDirectoryPath=<path>.

entries.name: WinMerge
entries.note: Two installer files: WinMerge-<ver>-x64-Setup.exe is machine-wide, WinMerge-<ver>-x64-PerUser-Setup.exe installs into %LocalAppData% - and winget defaults to the per-user one. Ship the plain x64-Setup.exe. Inno Setup; add /MERGETASKS="!desktopicon" to skip the desktop icon.

entries.name: ShareX
entries.note: Inno Setup. /NORUN is ShareX's own switch - without it ShareX launches when setup finishes. Run elevated (or as SYSTEM) it installs to Program Files; unelevated it goes per-user. Default tasks add Explorer context-menu and Send To entries and can take over the Print Screen key.

entries.name: IrfanView
entries.note: IrfanView's own installer - not Inno, not NSIS, so /S and /VERYSILENT do nothing. /allusers=1 only decides whether the shortcuts go to all users; leave it off under a deployment tool and they land in the SYSTEM profile. /assoc applies to the account that runs setup, so from SYSTEM it won't set file associations for your users - push those with a default-apps XML instead. Plugins are a separate installer.

entries.name: Everything (voidtools)
entries.note: By default the MSI installs and starts the Everything service (so standard users get instant NTFS search) and sets Everything to run at startup for all users. START_ON_STARTUP=0 stops the auto-run. The NSIS setup.exe takes /S instead.

entries.name: Bitwarden
entries.note: electron-builder NSIS. /allusers is REQUIRED for a machine-wide install - without it the app goes per-user, i.e. into the SYSTEM profile under a deployment tool. It is a WEB installer: the app itself downloads from GitHub during setup, so the endpoint needs to reach github.com. The uninstaller returns before it finishes (about 10 s in our lab). There is no MSI.

entries.name: draw.io
entries.note: Use draw.io-<ver>-windows-installer.exe (NSIS, machine-wide). The draw.io .msi - winget's default - is built as a per-user package. The uninstaller returns before it finishes (about 9 s in our lab).

entries.name: AWS CLI v2
entries.note: Use AWSCLIV2.msi. AWSCLIV2-User.msi is the per-user build, and AWS's newer install.ps1 is per-user too unless you pass -System. PATH changes only reach new shells.

entries.name: Azure CLI
entries.note: Use the -x64 MSI. The aka.ms/installazurecliwindows link Microsoft's quick-start uses is the 32-bit build, which lands in Program Files (x86). Installing the 64-bit MSI over it removes the 32-bit one, but CLI extensions then need reinstalling. Open a new shell before az is on PATH.

entries.name: PDF24 Creator
entries.note: Adds a "PDF24" virtual printer, registers PDF24 as a PDF reader and extends the Explorer right-click menu - each has a property to turn it off. Property values are Yes/No, not 1/0.

entries.name: OpenVPN Community
entries.note: The community client (OpenVPN GUI), not OpenVPN Connect. Installs the TAP / ovpn-dco network driver silently as SYSTEM with no driver prompt. Profiles go in C:\Program Files\OpenVPN\config (machine-wide) or %USERPROFILE%\OpenVPN\config; non-admin users need to be in the local "OpenVPN Administrators" group to start a connection from the GUI.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x64)
entries.note: One redistributable covers 2015 through 2022 (all 14.x). 32-bit apps need vc_redist.x86.exe as well, even on 64-bit Windows. Running an OLDER build where a newer one is installed exits 1638 (a newer version is already installed), which is success for a deployment. 3010 means a reboot is pending.

entries.name: Microsoft Windows Desktop Runtime 8 (x64)
entries.note: What WinForms / WPF apps built on .NET 8 need (HandBrake 1.11 is one); it is a different download from the ASP.NET Core runtime and the plain .NET runtime. It shows TWO entries in Add/Remove Programs, the bundle and the runtime; the bundle exe with /uninstall removed both in testing.

entries.name: HandBrake
entries.note: NSIS, so /S is case-sensitive. The installer carries no product name, so this matches on the file name. HandBrake 1.11 needs the .NET 8 Desktop Runtime: deploy that first (it was installed first in testing).

entries.name: Krita
entries.note: NSIS, so /S is case-sensitive. Installs to C:\Program Files\Krita (x64), which is where the uninstall string points.

entries.name: 1Password
entries.note: The MSI installed machine-wide as SYSTEM with no prompts. Each user still signs in to their own account after the install.

entries.name: Box Drive
entries.note: Machine-wide MSI. It registers in Add/Remove Programs as plain "Box", which matters if you detect or uninstall by name. Each user signs in to Box after the install.

entries.name: Box Tools
entries.note: Use BoxToolsInstaller-AdminInstall.msi, the admin build Box publishes alongside the regular BoxToolsInstaller.exe. It installed silently as SYSTEM with no prompts.

entries.name: Puppet Agent
entries.note: Set PUPPET_SERVER or the agent looks for a host literally named "puppet". Lab-tested with PUPPET_AGENT_STARTUP_MODE=Manual so the test VM did not try to check in; Automatic is what you want in production.

entries.name: Visual Studio 2010 Tools for Office Runtime (VSTO)
entries.note: Still required by many Office add-ins, including current ones. Installs two entries in Add/Remove Programs (10.0.60917 and a 10.0.60922 language pack). No uninstall string is published: msiexec /x on its product code hung as SYSTEM in testing, and a hanging uninstall is worse than none.

entries.name: Paint.NET
entries.note: Use the .winmsi download, which is an MSI inside a zip: unzip it and deploy the MSI.

entries.name: Amazon Corretto JDK (x64)
entries.note: Free OpenJDK build from Amazon, a common Oracle Java replacement. The MSI product name carries no Java version ("Amazon Corretto (x64)"), so check the version column, not the name, when you detect it.

entries.name: Amazon Corretto JRE 8 (x64)
entries.note: The Java 8 runtime only (no compiler), for old apps that still need Java 8 without an Oracle licence.

entries.name: PeaZip
entries.note: Inno Setup. The installer is NOT code-signed, so AppLocker or WDAC publisher rules will not allow it; allow it by hash or path instead.

entries.name: Brave
entries.note: Use the STANDALONE setup: the small default download fetches the browser at install time. Run as SYSTEM it installs machine-wide. The uninstall path contains the version number, so read it from the UninstallString in the registry. The uninstall exits 19, which Chromium-based installers use for a successful uninstall, not a failure.

entries.name: Inkscape
entries.note: The MSI is signed with Inkscape's own certificate, which Windows does not chain to a trusted root, so publisher-based allow rules will not match it.

entries.name: Nextcloud Desktop
entries.note: REBOOT=ReallySuppress keeps the install from rebooting the machine on its own. Each user connects their own Nextcloud account afterwards.

entries.name: DBeaver Community
entries.note: NSIS, so /S is case-sensitive. Add /allusers or it installs for one user only.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2013 Redistributable (x64)
entries.note: Older apps still need it; it installs side by side with 2015-2022. Microsoft names the download vcredist_x64.exe for every year, so this matches on the product name, not the file name.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2013 Redistributable (x86)
entries.note: For 32-bit apps, even on 64-bit Windows. Matches on the product name, because the file is just vcredist_x86.exe.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2012 Redistributable (x64)
entries.note: Update 4 (11.0.61030), the last 2012 build. Matches on the product name, because the file is just vcredist_x64.exe.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2010 Redistributable (x64)
entries.note: Different switches from the newer ones: 2010 takes /q, not /install /quiet, and is removed by its MSI product code (the one shown, for 10.0.40219 SP1 x64).

entries.name: Microsoft Windows Desktop Runtime 6 (x64)
entries.note: .NET 6 is out of Microsoft support; install it only for an app that still needs it. Shows two entries in Add/Remove Programs; the bundle exe with /uninstall removed both.

entries.name: Microsoft Windows Desktop Runtime 9 (x64)
entries.note: Shows two entries in Add/Remove Programs; the bundle exe with /uninstall removed both.

entries.name: Omnissa (VMware) Horizon Client
entries.note: Burn bundle; it installs USB redirection and other drivers, so plan a reboot. No uninstall string is published: removing it through its MSI returned 3010 and it stayed in Add/Remove Programs until a reboot, so treat removal as reboot-required.

entries.name: Lenovo System Update
entries.note: Inno Setup. It is a 32-bit app, so it installs under Program Files (x86). It installed and uninstalled cleanly on a non-Lenovo VM.

entries.name: PDF-XChange Editor
entries.note: Without a licence key it installs the free edition, which watermarks anything edited with the paid tools.

entries.name: SQL Server Management Studio 20
entries.note: SSMS 20 is the last Burn-bundle release; SSMS 21 and later install through the Visual Studio installer with different switches. The uninstall was tested through the copy Burn caches under C:\ProgramData\Package Cache, which is the same file and switches.

entries.name: TreeSize Free
entries.note: Inno Setup. /ALLUSERS matters - winget's default is a per-user install into %LocalAppData%\Programs. The download is TreeSizeFreeSetup.exe with no version in the name, so record which version you packaged.

entries.name: Dell Command | Update
entries.note: A Dell Update Package. Run on its own it exited 4 and installed nothing: 4 is the DUP code for a hard dependency, and DCU 5.x needs the .NET 8 Desktop Runtime. Deploy that runtime first and the same command installs cleanly, even on a non-Dell machine. The uninstall product code shown is for 5.7.0; read the current one from Add/Remove Programs for other versions.

entries.name: Microsoft Remote Desktop client (MSRDC)
entries.note: The client for Azure Virtual Desktop and Windows 365. ALLUSERS=1 is what makes it a machine-wide install; leave it off and the MSI installs for one user. It shows in Add/Remove Programs as just "Remote Desktop".

entries.name: Google Earth Pro
entries.note: There is no /S or /silent: OMAHA=1 is the property that runs the setup silently. Underneath it is an MSI, so it is removed by product code (the one shown is for 7.3.7.1327).

entries.name: Devolutions Remote Desktop Manager
entries.note: A plain machine-wide MSI with no required properties. It is about 350 MB, so stage it close to the endpoints rather than pulling it over a WAN link for every machine.

entries.name: mRemoteNG
entries.note: Use the MSI from the GitHub release, not the portable zip. Connection files live in each user's profile, so uninstalling the app does not remove anyone's saved connections.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2012 Redistributable (x86)
entries.note: Update 4 (11.0.61030). Same switches as the x64 package; 32-bit apps need this one even on 64-bit Windows, so many machines carry both.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2010 Redistributable (x86)
entries.note: Like the 2010 x64 package it takes /q, not /install /quiet, and is removed by its MSI product code (the one shown, for 10.0.40219 SP1 x86).

entries.name: Microsoft ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server
entries.note: IACCEPTMSODBCSQLLICENSETERMS=YES is required for a silent install. It also needs the Visual C++ 2015-2022 x64 runtime; the lab VM already had one, so deploy the runtime first on a clean image. Driver 18 encrypts connections by default, unlike 17, so test connection strings before replacing 17.

entries.name: Microsoft Azure Storage Explorer
entries.note: Inno Setup. With /ALLUSERS it installed machine-wide under Program Files, which is what a fleet deploy wants; keep it, since Inno installers that allow per-user installs can otherwise land in a single profile.

entries.name: Microsoft Access Database Engine 2016 Redistributable (x64)
entries.note: The ACE OLE DB and ODBC drivers that Excel and Access imports need on machines without Office. Microsoft's installer refuses to put the x64 engine next to 32-bit Office (and the x86 one next to 64-bit Office), so match the bitness of any Office already installed. It is removed by product code; the one shown is the English x64 package.

entries.name: Microsoft OLE DB Driver 19 for SQL Server
entries.note: IACCEPTMSOLEDBSQLLICENSETERMS=YES is required for a silent install. Version 19 installs side by side with 18 under a new provider name (MSOLEDBSQL19), so connection strings must be changed to use it, and like ODBC Driver 18 it encrypts connections by default.

entries.name: Microsoft .NET 8 Hosting Bundle
entries.note: The .NET and ASP.NET Core runtimes plus the ASP.NET Core Module for IIS, for servers that host .NET web apps. Install IIS first: if IIS is added later, run the bundle again with /repair so the module registers. OPT_NO_X86=1 skips the 32-bit runtimes.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2008 Redistributable (x64)
entries.note: 2008 SP1 with the MFC security update (9.0.30729.6161), the one old line-of-business apps still ask for. The package takes /q only (/install /quiet came with later years) and is removed by its MSI product code, shown for this version.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2008 Redistributable (x86)
entries.note: Same /q switch as the x64 package. 32-bit apps need this one even on 64-bit Windows, so many machines carry both. Removed by product code, shown for 9.0.30729.6161.

entries.name: TightVNC
entries.note: The full install puts a VNC server on the machine, so set the password properties in the same command (the lab run did) or install only the viewer with ADDLOCAL=Viewer. VNC passwords are capped at 8 characters, so also limit port 5900 to admin networks.

entries.name: TortoiseGit
entries.note: Installs cleanly without Git for Windows, but it does nothing useful until Git is there, so deploy Git first.

entries.name: R for Windows
entries.note: Inno Setup. /ALLUSERS puts it in Program Files for everyone. Each R version installs into its own R-x.y.z folder and leaves earlier versions in place, so the uninstall path changes with every release. RStudio Desktop is a separate install that failed as SYSTEM in the lab (exit 666660 from its elevation plugin), so it is not listed.

entries.name: Advanced IP Scanner
entries.note: The EXE is an Inno wrapper around an MSI, so it installs with Inno switches but must be removed with msiexec: its registered uninstall is MsiExec /X{code}, which sat on an invisible dialog as SYSTEM when given /VERYSILENT. The install also starts the app afterwards (in the lab it ran as SYSTEM), so end advanced_ip_scanner.exe after a deploy. Product code shown is for 2.5.4594.1.

entries.name: HWiNFO64
entries.note: Inno Setup. Its uninstaller is unins001.exe, not the usual unins000.exe, so read the path from Add/Remove Programs rather than guessing it.

entries.name: CPU-Z
entries.note: Inno Setup, installed machine-wide under Program Files\CPUID. Use the installer (cpu-z_x.xx-en.exe), not the zip, if you want it in Add/Remove Programs.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x86)
entries.note: Releases from 14.50 register in Add/Remove Programs as "Microsoft Visual C++ v14 Redistributable (x86)", not "2015-2022", so a detection rule that looks for the old name misses every up-to-date machine. 32-bit apps need this one even on 64-bit Windows.

entries.name: Dropbox
entries.note: Use the offline installer. With plain /S it installed machine-wide in about four minutes as SYSTEM; an older build run with /S /NOLAUNCH hung past 20 minutes in an earlier lab run. The registered uninstall carries /InstallType:MACHINE, which is what removes a machine-wide install.

entries.name: MobaXterm
entries.note: Download the Installer edition, not the Portable one. The zip holds the MSI and MobaXterm_installer.dat, which carries most of the payload (32 MB against a 14 MB MSI), so deploy the two files together from the same folder.

entries.name: UltraVNC
entries.note: Inno Setup. To choose components (viewer only, or server with your settings), record the choices once with /SAVEINF="setup.inf" on a test machine and replay them with /LOADINF="setup.inf".

entries.name: Microsoft Build of OpenJDK 21
entries.note: A plain MSI. To set JAVA_HOME and PATH as part of the install, add ADDLOCAL=FeatureMain,FeatureEnvironment,FeatureJarFileRunWith,FeatureJavaHome.

entries.name: Oracle JDK 21
entries.note: Check the licence on the exact update you package: Oracle offers JDK 21 free under its No-Fee Terms only for a year after the next LTS release, and later 21 updates move to the OTN licence, which is not free for production use. The Microsoft Build of OpenJDK installs the same way with no such terms.

entries.name: Logi Options+
entries.note: The installer is a bootstrapper that downloads the app: the 2.8 download installed 2.9, so machines need internet access and you cannot pin a version this way. /analytics no turns usage analytics off.

entries.name: Royal TS
entries.note: A plain machine-wide MSI with no required properties. It registers as "Royal TS V7" and is about 260 MB, so stage it close to the endpoints.

entries.name: Beyond Compare 5
entries.note: Inno Setup, and /ALLUSERS is required: without it the setup sat for more than eight minutes as SYSTEM and had to be killed; with it the install finished in seconds and registered as "Beyond Compare 5 (All users)". The licence key is entered separately.

entries.name: TechSmith Camtasia
entries.note: Deploy the Visual C++ 2015-2022 x64 runtime first: Camtasia 26.2 refuses to install unless it is 14.51.36231 or newer, and a silent install reports that only as exit 1603. Its MSI log says "Camtasia requires Microsoft Visual C++ 2019 Redistributable package v14.51.36231 or later". With a current runtime the same command installed and uninstalled cleanly.

entries.name: Arduino IDE
entries.note: A dual-purpose MSI (ALLUSERS=2, MSIINSTALLPERUSER=1) that defaults to a per-user install. Run as SYSTEM without ALLUSERS=1 it exited 1603 and installed nothing; with it, it installed into Program Files for every user. To change the folder use APPLICATIONFOLDER="C:\Apps\ArduinoIDE"; INSTALLDIR is ignored by this package. Admin install (/a) only unpacks files, it does not install.
